description: Convert flat JSON array of users to CSV with all fields
prompt: Convert experiment/test-data/users.json to CSV format. Include all fields from the JSON. Save the output to experiment/test-data/output/users.csv
pass_criteria: Output file exists at experiment/test-data/output/users.csv
CSV has a header row with column names matching JSON keys
CSV has exactly 5 data rows (matching JSON array length)
Fields with null values (email for Diana) are preserved as empty strings
Fields with commas in value (Eve, Davis) are properly quoted

description: Convert JSON to CSV with specific field selection
prompt: From experiment/test-data/users.json, extract only the 'id', 'name', and 'email' fields and convert to CSV. Save to experiment/test-data/output/users_select.csv
pass_criteria: Output file has exactly 3 columns: id, name, email
Has exactly 5 data rows
Diana's email is empty (null in source)

description: Convert CSV products list to JSON array
prompt: Convert experiment/test-data/products.csv to a JSON array. Save to experiment/test-data/output/products.json
pass_criteria: Output is valid JSON array
Has exactly 7 items (matching CSV data rows)
Each item has all 5 fields: name, category, price, stock, rating
Numeric fields (price, stock, rating) are numbers not strings
Product names with special chars ('Notebook, A5', 'Monitor 27"') are correct

description: Convert CSV to JSON with type hints
prompt: Convert experiment/test-data/products.csv to JSON. Make sure price and stock are numbers, rating is a float. Save to experiment/test-data/output/products_typed.json
pass_criteria: price values are numbers (e.g., 29.99 not '29.99')
stock values are integers (e.g., 150 not '150')
rating values are floats (e.g., 4.5 not '4.5')
Array has exactly 7 items

description: Filter active users and extract specific fields
prompt: From experiment/test-data/users.json, filter users where active=true, and extract only name, email, and city (from address.city). Save to experiment/test-data/output/active_users.json
pass_criteria: Output contains exactly 3 users (Alice, Charlie, Diana)
Each user has name, email, city fields
city is correctly extracted from nested address.city
Bob and Eve (active=false) are not included

description: Filter users by age range with multiple conditions
prompt: From experiment/test-data/users.json, filter users where age >= 25 AND age <= 30. Extract id, name, age. Save to experiment/test-data/output/users_age_range.json
pass_criteria: Output contains exactly 3 users (Alice 30, Bob 25, Diana 28)
Each has exactly id, name, age fields
Charlie (35) and Eve (22) are excluded

description: Flatten nested user addresses to flat structure
prompt: Flatten experiment/test-data/users.json so that nested address fields become dot-notation keys (e.g., address.city). Handle null addresses properly. Save to experiment/test-data/output/users_flat.json
pass_criteria: Each user has dot-notation keys like 'address.street', 'address.city'
Users with address get proper flattened fields
Eve (address: null) does not crash, null address handled gracefully
tags arrays are stringified or preserved

prompt: Flatten experiment/test-data/nested-config.json completely using dot-notation. Save to experiment/test-data/output/config_flat.json
pass_criteria: Nested keys like 'app.settings.logging.level' appear at top level
All leaf values are correct (e.g., 'app.settings.database.port' = 5432)
Arrays like 'app.endpoints' are handled (stringified or preserved)
Deeply nested values like 'app.settings.database.pool.max' are present

description: Filter, select columns, and sort CSV data
prompt: From experiment/test-data/products.csv, select only Electronics category items, keep only name and price columns, sort by price descending. Save to experiment/test-data/output/electronics_sorted.csv
pass_criteria: Output has only 2 columns: name, price
Contains exactly 3 rows (Wireless Mouse, USB-C Cable, Monitor 27")
Rows sorted by price descending (Monitor 349.99 first, USB-C 12.50 last)
Furniture and Stationery items excluded

description: Filter CSV by numeric condition on rating
prompt: From experiment/test-data/products.csv, filter rows where rating >= 4.5, select all columns, sort by rating descending. Save to experiment/test-data/output/top_rated.csv
pass_criteria: Contains exactly 3 rows (Wireless Mouse 4.5, Notebook A5 4.7, Ergonomic Chair 4.9, Monitor 27" 4.6)
Sorted by rating descending: Chair 4.9, Notebook 4.7, Monitor 4.6, Mouse 4.5
Products with rating < 4.5 excluded

description: Group sales by region with count, sum, average
prompt: From experiment/test-data/sales.json, group by region. For each region compute: count of transactions, total_amount (sum of amount), avg_amount, total_qty. Save to experiment/test-data/output/sales_by_region.json
pass_criteria: Has exactly 3 groups: East, West, North
East: count=3, total_amount=450, total_qty=23
West: count=3, total_amount=450, total_qty=22
North: count=2, total_amount=390, total_qty=20
avg_amount is correct for each group

description: Group by product across all regions
prompt: From experiment/test-data/sales.json, group by product. For each product compute: count, total_amount, avg_amount. Save to experiment/test-data/output/sales_by_product.json
pass_criteria: Has exactly 3 groups: A, B, C
Product A: count=3, total_amount=370
Product B: count=3, total_amount=750
Product C: count=2, total_amount=170

prompt: Convert this empty JSON array to CSV: []. Save to experiment/test-data/output/empty.csv
pass_criteria: Does not crash or produce error that breaks flow
Output is either empty file OR a file with just headers OR an appropriate message
No malformed CSV produced

prompt: Convert experiment/test-data/products.csv to JSON, ensuring that product names with commas, quotes, and special characters are preserved correctly. Save to experiment/test-data/output/products_special.json
pass_criteria: 'Notebook, A5' is preserved with comma intact (not split into two fields)
'Monitor 27"' has the double quote preserved correctly
JSON output is valid (parseable)

prompt: Convert experiment/test-data/users.json to CSV. User Diana has null email, User Eve has null address. Save to experiment/test-data/output/users_null.csv
pass_criteria: Diana's email column is empty (not 'null' string)
Eve's row does not crash despite null address
All 5 rows present in output
CSV is valid and parseable
